title: kb pack reads a commit in batches
summary: kb pack now reads a commit with a fixed number of git processes, whatever its file count: one listing for .ia/src, one for the selection's other paths, and one cat-file --batch read for each, instead of two processes per file. On a 124-file tree a pack starts 7 git processes instead of 254 and takes about 3 to 5 s instead of 22 to 24 s, with a byte-identical package. Every path is still checked in order with the same refusals; a repository missing an object it would not have read (a partial clone) falls back to reading path by path. The legacy committed writer is unchanged.
